items.title: Document the current failure mode and scope boundary
items.context: Use the verified evidence: lattice.config.json validate.commands is a subset, verifier skips npm test fallback when configured commands exist, TEST writes test-evidence from lattice validate, DONE consumes test-evidence only, and pre-push is build/tsc rather than full npm test. This story writes the execution plan only and must not implement runtime gate code.

happy.desc: The document cites the verified current failure mode: validate.commands subset, verifier fallback suppression, TEST test-evidence write, DONE test-evidence consumption, and pre-push not running root npm test.

edge.desc: The document clearly states that this does not prove current main npm test is red; it proves the gate can miss failures outside validate.commands.

adversarial.desc: The document keeps runtime implementation, lattice.config.json command edits, and running full npm test out of this planning story scope.

verificationEvidence.note: Document lines state the 8 configured validate commands, 22-step root npm test chain, verifier fallback suppression, TEST test-evidence write, DONE test-evidence consumption, and pre-push not running root npm test.

items.title: Specify the target gate design and rollout plan
items.context: Plan a robust solution such as DONE/release validation profile or doneRequiredCommands with fresh hash-bound evidence, self-host default requiring root npm test, external project configurability, emergency handling, migration, and false-positive/de-escalation policy.

happy.desc: The document specifies a target DONE/release validation profile or equivalent doneRequiredCommands design with fresh hash-bound evidence and a dedicated DONE row.

edge.desc: The design distinguishes Orchestrate self-host defaults from external project opt-in/configurable behavior so ordinary users are not forced into root npm test cost.

adversarial.desc: The design rejects prompt-only policy and requires schema, runner, process-fact, done-oracle, smoke, docs, and migration touchpoints for implementation.

items.title: Record validation and 3 round / 2 host audit requirements
items.context: Because this affects Lattice core DONE semantics, the plan must include concrete smoke tests, minimal commands, expected artifacts, and mandatory 3 round / 2 host review before implementation.

happy.desc: The document lists concrete implementation verification commands, expected artifacts, and smoke scenarios that prove subset validate cannot unlock DONE when full-suite evidence is missing or failing.

edge.desc: The document defines in-flight story migration, emergency bypass/degraded handling, and stale evidence recovery without weakening DONE semantics.

adversarial.desc: The document mandates 3 distinct rounds with 2 independent hosts over the final material hash for implementation of this high-risk gate change.
